result:
Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (5/5; the 422 stack trace in the output is pre-existing noise from the starter `posts.search` test), and repeat runs stay green.

`DashboardController.index` (app/Http/Controllers/DashboardController.ts) now also queries the signed-in user's own posts — `postCount` via `Post.newQuery().where('authorId', …).count()` and `recentPosts` via the same scoped query ordered `createdAt desc, id desc` (the id tiebreak matters because SQLite stores `created_at` as a string, so same-second posts would otherwise be unordered) limited to 5, mapped to `{ id, title }` — and passes both props alongside the existing `user` to the page; guests still get 0 / `[]`, though the auth middleware redirects them first. `resources/js/pages/dashboard/Index.tsx` takes the two new props and renders, below the "Signed in as" panel, a `You have N posts` line (singular for 1) plus a "Recent posts" list of Inertia `Link`s to `route('posts.show', { id })`, falling back to "You haven't written any posts yet." with a link to the new-post form when the list is empty; `.guren/pages.gen.ts` was regenerated by `bun run codegen` to pick up the new Props shape. I added `tests/DashboardController.test.ts`, which migrates the test database, creates a fresh author plus a second user, and asserts the guest redirect, the count of 7 with exactly the five newest titles newest-first, and that the other user's post never appears on the author's dashboard.
